title: AI is a major security threat, spy chiefs warn cabinet
source_used: International Business Times Singapore (relaying The Sunday Times); the thetimes.com page returned no text
key_facts: MI5 director general Sir Ken McCallum, MI6 chief Blaise Metreweli and GCHQ director Anne Keast-Butler briefed the cabinet in a regular assessment of the national threat picture, according to a report by The Sunday Times relayed by International Business Times Singapore.
McCallum reportedly told ministers that AI was 'the biggest thing you should be thinking about'.
The meeting was not prompted by an imminent danger but included an extended discussion of how hostile actors, including Russia and Iran, terrorist groups and individuals, could exploit AI.
One cabinet minister reportedly compared the situation with the early stages of the COVID pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis, when warning signs were visible but limited action followed.

Government 'hackathons' this summer, run by the Government Cyber Co-ordination Centre, found 407 security vulnerabilities across nine government organisations, one rated critical; the exercises cost about 13,000 pounds.
A government spokesman said national security is the first duty of government and that Britain must prepare by testing advanced systems, building domestic capabilities and 'hardening our defences'.
quote_evidence: Sir Ken McCallum, the MI5 director general, reportedly told ministers that AI was "the biggest thing you should be thinking about".

The meeting was not prompted by an imminent danger, but included an extended discussion about how AI could be exploited by hostile actors, including Russia and Iran, as well as terrorist organizations and individuals.
During a series of government "hackathons" this summer, the Government Cyber Co-ordination Centre uncovered 407 security vulnerabilities across nine government organisations.
why_it_matters_hint: The heads of Britain's three main intelligence agencies reportedly rank AI misuse among the country's top security worries.
event_date: Cabinet briefing date not confirmed (the relay says 8 Sep 2026); The Sunday Times report published 10 Oct 2026
notes: The Times page (thetimes.com) returned HTTP 200 but no article text (subscription wall), so the text was read through International Business Times Singapore, which credits The Sunday Times. The relay gives the briefing date as 8 Sep, which looks doubtful, so the entry gives no date. Google News lists the Times item at 10 Oct 2026 20:00 UTC.
